models.purpose: Reduce people, technology and process to sixteen sub-indicators, ten of them with an explicit formula.
models.summary: People gets six indicators: multi-workforce from a questionnaire, proficiency as work per time, ability as data per staff, turnover as the leaving share, experience as average tenure, education as an average of scored levels. Technology gets downtime, mean time to repair, a cost breakdown with no formula, relevance with no formula, and a product count with no formula. Process gets accuracy, an unformulated consistency, repeatability, a maintenance rate, and a self-scored data masking.

models.purpose: Map every indicator so that larger means more mature, weight the three groups and the indicators by the analytic hierarchy process, and return one maturity score in [0, 100].
models.summary: Three maps are declared: a hyperbolic tangent for indicators whose rise helps, an exponential for indicators whose rise hurts, and the identity where no map is needed. Pairwise judgement matrices, one 3 by 3 and three smaller ones, give a principal eigenvector that is normalized into weights, accepted only when the consistency ratio stays under 0.1. Mapped values are multiplied by 100, combined within each group, then combined across groups. The result is read on five equal bands of twenty points.

models.purpose: Rank the sixteen indicators by a PageRank on their causal network so the advice knows what to improve first.
models.summary: Indicators are nodes and a causal influence is an edge. An initial distribution over the sixteen nodes is updated by the share of each neighbour's rank divided by that neighbour's out-degree, then damped by a teleportation term so the rank cannot get trapped. The indicator with the largest rank is improved first.

governing_equations.purpose: Add the teleportation term.

constraints: The sixteen initial ranks sum to one.

details: The initial ranks over the sixteen indicators sum to one.

assumptions: A rise in one indicator can move another, and that link is stable enough to draw.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Figure 3 draws the network, but no rank is computed and the damping is never given a value.

validation_refs: Figure 3 shows the sixteen-node network coloured by group.
models.computational_cost: A sixteen-by-sixteen iteration; negligible if run.
strengths: The teleportation term stops rank collecting in a node with no outgoing edge.
The ranking turns the advice into an order rather than a list.
limitations: The prose calls the ranks the values of each word, a slip carried over from the text-ranking source.
No computed rank is shown, so the advice in section 4.2 is not actually ordered by this model.

models.purpose: Treat data transmission as an M/M/infinity queue and read off the expected volume in the system.
models.summary: Data are the customers and the system is the server, with infinitely many servers. Arrivals are Poisson with rate lambda and service is exponential with mean one over mu, first come first served. Balancing the flow between neighbouring states gives the stationary distribution, and the expected number in the system is lambda over mu.

models.purpose: Measure the data cascade by an average degree and by the sum of network diameters, then grade the system with five protocol rules.
models.summary: Copies of data are vertices and a cascade between two copies is an edge. The cascade level is the sum of the total degrees divided by the vertex counts, and the cascade speed uses the sum of the diameters. The protocol then grades the processing speed from a tail probability, the cascade level against a reference, and the cascade speed as the reciprocal of that sum, averages the three, and reads the result on four bands.

models.purpose: Model the share of customers who adopt the metric with a replicator equation driven by the gap between benefit and cost.
models.summary: Adopters earn alpha minus beta and everyone else earns nothing, so the benefit is alpha times the adopter share. The replicator dynamics then say the share grows exactly when the benefit beats the cost, and the paper plots the benefit over time for three benefits and three costs.

strengths: The threshold falls straight out of the equation: the share grows only when alpha exceeds beta.

dependency_edges.handoff: The sixteen sub-indicators, ten computed and six self-scored, are the values the three maps and the two-layer weighting turn into the maturity.
The maturity and the group scores fix which indicators are weak, and the causal network ranks which of them to improve first.
The arrival rate, the service rate and the expected volume supply the processing-speed rule that the protocol averages with the two cascade measures.
